steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

In a medium bowl, cream together the butter, brown sugar, and white sugar. Mix in the eggs and vanilla. Combine the flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt; add to butter mixture, and stir until just blended. With a large wooden spoon, stir in the white, milk, and semi-sweet chocolate chips. Stir in the walnuts, pecans, and almonds. Drop dough by heaping spoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes in the preheated oven. Allow cookies to cool on the baking sheet before transferring to wire racks to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Stephen's Chocolate Chip Cookies
raw_recipe.description: I created this recipe for my father on his birthday. It contains lots of different chocolates and nuts. Thanks Dad for sending me to cookie baking school at the San Francisco Culinary Academy! This one is just for you!
raw_recipe.name: Stephen's Chocolate Chip Cookies

review.reviewBody: EXCELLENT! All my friends ask for this recipe. I make large batches, make the cookie balls, flash freeze them and store them in a zip loc bag to bake a few at a time at a later date.

I prefer these over most of the cookie recipes on here, although like the other ones I found them to be too sweet so I used 1C brown sugar and only 1/2 of white sugar. That made them near perfect. They are thinner cookies and spread quite a bit, so space them well!

I made a few "tweaks" because this is the closest recipe to one I use to know. I melt the butter. I only use dark and milk chocolate chips and walnuts. I mix the flour, baking soda and powder together in one bowl, eggs, add melted butter, and vanilla mix with blender, both sugars and mix with blender again. I then quarter the flour mixture and fold in with a rubber spatula. Finally add the chips and nuts and bake! This makes them even more moist!!!

These cookies are bomb! They are so good and totally recommend. I didn't use the nuts but they were still amazing. I added a bit of espresso powder to have more flavors come through. I added 1 tsp and it worked out perfectly. There wasn't any coffee flavor but strengthened the others.

My whole family LOVES these cookies!! I’ve made so many chocolate chip, M&M, Oatmeal Chocolate Chip, and so many more cookies with this recipe! The cookie is so yummy and it doesn’t take too long to make. I also like this recipe because you can add whatever you want into it! It’s not like a Snickerdoodle where the only thing good in it is cinnamon. You can add M&M’s, oatmeal, chocolate chips, Reese’s Pieces, and more. The only change I made was I altered the cooking time from 10-12 minutes to 15 minutes. Absolutely amazing cookies.

Good recipe. I didn't use all the different chips and nuts this time. I used Ghirardelli milk chocolate chips and pecans. They turned out great. I did bake for 11 mins in a 350 degree oven. Ten minutes just wasn't enough and 12 was too much, oddly one more minute made the difference.

SOOO GOOOODD. I've made these cookies a lot of times and i loved them. My family always asks me to make them when guests come over. I would really recommend to wait 12 minutes stick a toothpick in one of the cookies. If little crumb-like bits appear on the toothpick and the toothpick is hot and soft (just a little before it fully bakes), take it out and don't take the cookies off of the pan to let them bake outside the oven. After 5-7 minutes, take them off and let them cool. Trust me, if you do this you will get a soft, chewy cookie.

The cookies taste great. Leave out the baking powder as it makes them cakey. not crisp (I tried both ways). Also, reduce white sugar to about 1/4C - that's enough. 
But can anyome tell me how to keep the dough from sticking to my tbsp-sized ice cream scoop?
These cookies were SO good. I added 2 cups of flour and half a cup of cocoa powder to make double chocolate chip cookies because I couldn't find a super good one, but they were SO good either way.
I added a small box of vanilla pudding to the mix. They are awesome and I know my grandkids will love them if my husband can leave them alone long enough...

YUM! I am so glad that I followed this recipe EXACTLY. I was tempted to change it due to some of the bad reviews. I don't see why people thought these were flat. Mine turned out just like a cookie should. Yes, they are sweet, but not overly so. I didn't pack my brown sugar, because the recipe didn't say to. I also stirred the flour into the butter / sugar mixture (this is how I read the recipe), rather than using mixer at this step. I don't know if mixing would have produced a flatter cookie?! Also, I put the dough in the fridge between cooking and cooked for 9 min. which seemed perfect. I also let them cool on cookie sheet about 9 min. before transfering to cooking rack. Lastly, I didn't soften butter as long as I usually do when a recipe calls for softened butter. Mine was pretty chilled. I just had to mix a little more to get it creamed with the sugar. SOOOOO.... I have no idea if any of this might have made the difference in the final result of the cookie, but this was a perfect chocolate chip cookie in my eyes (and in my tummy)! Like others, I usually am underwhelmed with chocolate chip cookie recipes, and keep trying to find one I like, THIS IS IT!!
Turned out perfectly - were not flat like others said.

Good but flat. The taste was good but even after putting one batch of dough in the fridge for at least 15 minutes, they still came out flat and crispy. I did run out of white sugar though, so used mainly all brown sugar which may have caused the difference.
Easy, a little too much chocolate.

I always struggle with cookies going hard wether or not I put straight to a plate,use a cooling rack leave on the stove, leave on the sheet off the stove. I can NEVER get it right. I fully expected tha result when I come back from a nap after leaving them to cool and they were SOFT and so super yummy! best cookie I've ever made (I only did reg.semi sweet chips and a few leftover milk ones and also I was short 1c.white sugar so I used an extra cup of brown) best best BEST chocolate chip recipe I've made and I've attempted many!
I was so happy I had to come and leave a review (which I've never done ha!)! thanks for sharing!
great cookie but way too much butter...will use half next time

This recipe is excellent, hands down. I’ve tried numerous recipes and they are always mediocre. I followed the recipe as-is, and then changed it up with whatever chips I was in the mood for. Wonderful.

Great cookies. Made an impromptu 1/2 batch due to limited ingredients on hand and split that into a dozen choc chip only and dozen with nuts. Delicious. As others said, crispy edge but soft center which is my favorite. Not too greasy and not too cake-like. Definitely my go-to from now on! Thx!
I LOVE THESE AND IF YOU DON’T HAVE THE NUTS AND OTHER CHOCOLATE IT IS STILL AMAZING!
Awesome!
